source_en: Shall I tell you the story of the Crimson Moon? Yes, you Nephilim love this story. Your story. Long ago, we lived under a Golden Age. source_en: You see them as monsters; I see them differently, as the true heirs to the Throne your god slumbers upon. If you knew the things I did, you’d lay your weapons down, or turn them to where they rightfully belong.

source_en: The Dead Gods are no different than yours. The victors simply wrote the history books. Another war, another cultural conflict, resulting in a world divorced from reality. Humans are merely narrative animals; they care not for what truly is, but for how something feels. Truth breaks man, but for one over man, like a Nephilim perhaps, it can ignite a fire

source_en:
Mathias. 

I implore you to heed my warnings about these heretics. No longer can we stand idly while these “Reborn” further lead your flock astray. While I can appreciate your reservations during these dire times, the Archbishop entrusted you with the well-being of Gildenarch’s faithful. The city needs no less than an inquisition to rout these iconoclasts. We have an opportunity to stamp out this madness before it spreads throughout Velchoria, a failure to stain the chapter for generations I'm sure. 

I know you have what it takes to save the souls of Gildenarch’s people. Do not let our efforts in her restoration be for naught.

Faithfully yours, S M

source_en:
In the hunt for Aegoroth, Eye of the Abyss, I grow closer. A resident from the Inn claims to have come across a most peculiar people. Just three days journey from here. To hear him say it, during his travels in the Armaea Hills he came across a small wooden structure, what he thought was a church. Upon closer inspection, he found the building empty. 

Being a storm coming, he decided to shelter for the night. It must have been the lightning that saved him--for he awoke startled by the flash and in that wisp of light, he found men standing all around him, spread about in a fanning circle, all watching him sleep, all with empty hollows where there should be eyes.

Just like that, the light passed and he was left in the dark. And when the next flash came-they were gone. It is said that devout followers relinquish their eyes to Aegoroth for just a glimpse of his flesh. Lunacy. Fanatics. Obviously. But still, a fantastic opportunity for a firsthand interview! They must know more about the lost legends of this fabled creature than any.  

I shall begin my journey tomorrow.

في رحلة مطاردة إيقوروث، عين الهاوية، أقترب أكثر. يدعي أحد نزلاء النزل أنه صادف قوماً في غاية الغرابة. على بعد ثلاثة أيام فقط من هنا. وبحسب قوله، فخلال رحلاته في تلال أرميا، عثر على هيكل خشبي صغير، ظن أنه كنيسة. وعند فحص المبنى عن كثب، وجده خالياً. 

ولما أقبلت عاصفة، آثر أن يبيت فيه. لا بد أن البرق هو ما أنقذه، فقد استيقظ فجأة على ومضة الضوء، وفي ذلك الخيط من النور، وجد رجالاً يقفون حوله، منتشرين في حلقة متسعة، كلهم يرقب نومه، وفي محاجرهم فراغٌ حيث ينبغي أن تكون العيون. 

وهكذا، مر الضوء وتركه في الظلام. وعندما جاءت الومضة التالية، اختفوا. يقال إن الأتباع الورعين يتخلون عن أعينهم لإيقوروث مقابل لمحة واحدة من جسده. جنون. تعصّب. بلا ريب. ولكن مع ذلك، هي فرصة رائعة لإجراء مقابلة مباشرة! ولا بد أنهم أعلم الناس بأساطير هذا المخلوق الضائعة. 

سأبدأ رحلتي غداً.

The time has come, Mathias. We have belayed our response long enough. The disorder and chaos that we’ve allowed to fester within the city has now justified extreme action.  

In fact, the people hunger for it. They yearn for the strength of the iron hand. 

Even the worst heresy, sometimes, is an act in service to the greater good.  And make no mistake, there is no greater good without evil.  No advancement without destruction. No immortality without death.  

The death of others, at least.

As prefect of the Doctrine, you've done your part, your Emminence. Now we will do ours.

The people have asked for the touch of the iron hand.

Now, Mathias, we will give them what they want. 

-Solomon.

PS: The Divine has Infernus to banish souls to. We have Shoreditch Prison.

source_en:
What a cruel and undeserved fate, oh beautiful E’frae. Whose green ran through the earth, whose voice was whispered among the wind, and whose love gave rise to life every spring.

 I mourn your loss, great father of the wild, but I cannot join you in the Rot. I will journey far from these lands to the region of Western Armaea. Far from the Church’s clutches, I will plant your seed and tend to it as your wisdom tended to my soul.

The Saedric memory will live on even in this darkened age. Farewell, my father; I will carry you with me in all things I do.

source_en:
Asher,

The bolt on my study door is a brass thing of poor manufacture, three-pin tumbler, replaced in the autumn of '02 by Greaves, who did the work for a guinea and complained the entire afternoon. I mention it because tonight I am grateful for it, which is more consideration than the bolt has ever earned.

Three chairs at the Fellow's Council are empty now. Marvenne. Hollis. Old Korbel.

Marvenne told me last spring she had had words with Master Felwyl over his revised Eveirington reading list. He was, she said, unwilling to entertain disagreement. Two months later — sabbatical. The other two had complaints in similar weather, and now the registry tells me they are abroad.

Marvenne has no family abroad.

One other thing, and you may laugh. I have served at Elk Grove forty-one years. I know how the chapel candles burn. They have been burning low. Low when no one is in the hall. Low when the windows are shut.

I am not imagining it.

I will see you at the Gala. Do not approach me first. I will find you near the orchestra, between the second movement and the third, when no one is listening because everyone is listening.

Yours,
 H.

source_en:
The Dry Rot King, his people called it before the name was the last word any of them could still speak.

The Saedrics were his people: keepers of the old groves, who counted their years in harvests rather than kings. When their god began to rot in the dark, something of him reached back through the roots and into them. They did not die. They dried.
Now they are the Rot Kin, and they tend the forest the way grief tends a grave. The stone was never a prison so much as a wound stitched shut. It holds a god, but it does not heal him and it does not silence him. The wardens who guard it report the same thing across centuries,the longer he is kept, the less of E'frae remains, and the more of the rot answers in his place.

Where his influence reaches, the land does not burn or drown. It simply gives up. Leaves brown on a windless day. Timber crumbles though no rain has touched it. Animals lie down and do not rise again. It is not death, exactly, death is an ending, this is a slow forgetting of how to be alive.

source_en:
I heard the children singing in the courtyard today. A new rhyme lilting from their innocent little voices.  

At first I didn't understand what they were saying, but when I did, I brought them in and put them to work on their numbers, forbidding them to speak for the rest of the day.  

I copied down the rhyme here before I forgot, in case it's needed for evidence.  

The rhyme goes-

"Where the red rash spreads, comes the never dead. 
Where pain flees, sunlight never sees. 
Where old age goes, the devil knows. The devil knows. The devil knows."

And then there was a second part, which would surely be some form of heresy if the inquisitors ever heard it.

"To the church goes the tithes 
To the kingdom the taxes
To Hell goes the souls 
Who touch the Abraxas."

Halvern Room, half past the Tenth Bell. Knock twice, then once. Five of them — Devereaux, Halhurst, Old Pellaby, Tannig, Anderson.

Be brief. Be brief. Be brief.

Open with the joke about Halhurst's clocks. Clocks paid by the hour. Wait for the laugh. If they do not laugh, turn serious abruptly.

Then: the Church is exhausted... Sold its last seat three hundred years ago... No new pews... Nothing it could offer me would be enough even if it still had something to offer.

Tuesday. Botanical Studies, third hour. Eight of us, two missing — Wynn says it's the cough going around, but I never met anyone who liked Wynn enough to tell her where they actually were.

Master Felwyl brought a new specimen today. He carried it himself, which he never does. A small thing in a glass dome. Pale pink, with red veins. He said the name in old Lunitarian and I didn't catch it. I'll ask Cora. Cora always remembers.

He let us each look. Up close it pulses, very softly, like it is breathing. Master Felwyl said this was not breathing. He said it was simply sap. He smiled when he said it.

It is a little ugly. The stem is too white. But the flower is, I must admit, the loveliest thing I have ever seen. When I smelled it, my mouth watered, which is silly. I keep thinking about it. I keep thinking about it the way I would think about a boy.

Then the bell, and we filed out, and I forgot to copy the diagram from the board.

Oh — the Gala is on the Eve. Father bought me a sash. I look very serious in it. He laughed. I was offended, then I laughed.

I'll write of the party after.

source_en:
Monday. Fitting at Madame Auvern's at the Sixth Bell. Tea at Reverence Hall. The Devereaux woman is wearing crimson, of course she is, the woman has the imagination of a banker's wife. Sash for me, then; one cannot match.

Tuesday. The Cathedral Auxiliary, then dinner at the Haedriks. Edmund pleads his nerves and will not come. He has pled his nerves three weeks running. I am beginning to suspect his nerves know of nothing other than pleading.

Wednesday. Sat for my portrait. The painter remarked that the moon has been very red of late, and asked if I had noticed. I said the moon is not noticed if one is properly dressed.

Thursday. Lunch with Vivienne. She said two of her staff have given notice without explanation. I gave her mine. I have a girl from Pontoon Town who is grateful and quiet and has not yet had the chance to learn how to leave.

Friday. Confession. I lied about the usual things. Father Olm seemed distracted. I asked after his health. He said he had been sleeping poorly, and that the chapel candles were burning low.

The Eve. The Spire. Crimson sash. Eighth Bell. Carriage at the door.

I am told one must, on these occasions, smile.

Greetings, upon the Eve of the New Moon.

By the Grace of the Lunitarian Faith, the Industry of Gildenarch's Finest Hands, and the Generosity of Lord Solomon Moore — Your Presence is Requested at the Celebration of the Completion of the Godsreach Spire, that noble Edifice raised in the sight of Heaven, that the City might at last raise her Glass to a Future Earned.

The Programme:
Drinks at Sundown. Dinner in the Oratory Hall. Address by His Eminence, Cardinal Mathias. A Word from our Honored Patron.

The evening shall conclude with a Procession to the Threshold of the Spire, where the Doors shall open to those Benefactors, Fellows, Ministers, Patrons, and Distinguished Families of the Ward who have given so much to a City that has, at last, given itself back.

Black tie. Crimson sash. The carriage at the Eighth Bell.

R.S.V.P. before the moon turns.
The Doors close from within.

source_en:
My dear Wensleigh,

Two candles, and the second already crooked. You will forgive the haste. I write quickly because this evening, when it comes, will be very long.

You are a rare student. I do not say this to flatter you. I say it because the saying has become rare. Most who pass through my hall admire the lantern, and the pleasing circle of light it permits them. You have always been of a different garden, most content at the edges of the light.

I will speak briefly tonight. The Cardinal will speak longer. Our Patron will speak last, and the wine will be very fine, and you will be bored, and that is right and good.

After the toasts — when the older guests find the air heavy and retire to their carriages — find me. There is a smaller gathering for the few who have taken the trouble to look further. I have argued for your inclusion. The argument was not difficult. It rarely is, with you.

Wear something you can move in. Pin nothing to your collar that you would mourn.

Yours, in faith and in the better light to come,
 F.

What's reborn can be rekilled. Remember that, you fools. 

It's the cult that brought this down on all of us. I'd wager anything.

It was only me that ran. 

It’s important I write that here, so it’s recorded. I’d want no stench of desertion to be levied against the others, who fought bravely to a man. 

Their names should be clean, unlike mine—Daerun Bogmire, as it’s recorded in the sentry lists. A name, even bad as it is, that I couldn't live up to.

Goodbye.

source_en:
Gallant,
Your prose... beautiful as ever. 
But once again, all that comes of it are lies. Youth believes love can conquer all. But the books tell me otherwise. 
I waited under the willow. I watched the stars twinkle and fade. Fire to coal, my heart moved with them—as I realized, you were not coming. 
I cursed you. I even threw a book! Can you imagine? Of course I quickly dusted it off and set it back atop the shelf – what has The Traveling Tales of Tiverna ever done to me? 
But all of that was before I got the news. 
It’s worse than I feared. It’s not that you forgot me for one night. It’s that you’re gone forever, a fading star out of reach. 
I have no idea where you are, but your Officer says this will reach you. Of course I don’t believe him, but writing is a healing of its own.
Goodbye my love. 
We were young once.
Watching branches glitter the stars
But youth leaves us now 
As we leave each other naught but scars.

Your faded star,
Mereda

source_en:
An unorthodox exploration of Lunitarian myth and legend that scrutinizes the conventional narrative of Archangel Maedrael. A particular passage sticks out to you.

It could not be understated just how unlike men the High Daemons of Ludereon are. They are not corporeal beings but instead constructed of a sort of “Resonant Energy”. If records from the old world are to be believed, they’ve taken many forms, in fact.

 According to canon, the invention of Angelic Sigils, the magick used to give an Angel a particular form with attributes, comes directly from the Archangel himself—a puzzling detail if only canon is taken into account. If we consider my prior explorations, there may be more to Maedrael than we’ve come to believe. I propose a theory, one perhaps well outside of the realm of accepted thought, that Maedrael is not of Ludereon. How else can one possess the 'self directed will' akin to that of man?

source_en:
Lunarin is the Dragon! The Demiurge lives once more through the Church. A Millenia of Lies befell man after the Imperial Conversion. 

I have good news, brothers and sisters. Though our forefathers were deceived by the Lunitarians, there yet remains another way to freedom! Freedom from this earth, from suffering and pain, just as we were before the Demiurge ensared our souls in the Coil! The Initiated know the truth about Lost Akyreon, the realm of Aeons Given Flesh, who’ve been scorned by Archons of the Throne. Their unjust persecution is the fate of man should we continue to unwittingly serve the Dragon. 

The Church calls them Demons; we shall call them Shepherds! The Shepherds have given us a gift. 

Tonight we must accept their offering and partake in the powers of the realm beyond this accursed veil.

source_en: Forgive my hesitancy towards Felwyl’s spiritual claims; he was always an odd one. His interest in the occult, though not inherently a problem itself, does concern me. I knew a practitioner once, a woman named Mereda. She was an alumna of Elk Grove back in the day, and she, too, was a magician. A lovely woman whom I’d trust dearly, but I’ll always remember what she told me: “never trust a demon”. I know damn well what Felwyl’s been up to, and I’m sure that Solomon figure has something to do with it. The Flora Felwyl has been presenting to his students is not of this world; he’s obtained it from some unholy means, and I’d rather not be involved with it. Don’t bother getting the Archspire involved; their leniency towards the Aristocracy is what’s keeping this bloated pig's corpse of a city alive.

Your last reached me Tuesday. I've read it three times. The hand wasn't yours. I know your hand — eight years of it. The loops don't crowd like that, and you have never once spelt my name with the second N. 

Tell me you wrote it. Tell me your wrist is hurt and one of the kinder ones wrote for you. Tell me anything and I'll believe it, only write back in your own hand. 

I went to the gates yesterday with bread. The new Sister wouldn't take it. No visitors to the lower wards, she said. She wouldn't look at me. 

Lily asks for you every night. Write me. Write me in your own hand and I'll burn this. 

— Your Anya

source_en:
Solomon — 

You ask if I have the stomach. I have eaten venison while a poacher hung dripping from my rafters, keeping time with the strings. I do not lack stomach. 

The keep is yours. Take it down to the sea-stones if it pleases you. The lower wards too — I'm told the air there is rich, and that the men who survive long enough develop a most remarkable patience. 

You offer me red, and long red years to drink it. I accept. I would have signed for the offer alone, without the keep — but you are a man of style, and I shall not deprive you of the pleasure of payment. 

I'll be at the Aemar after the second course. Have something young ready. The first hunger, I'm told, is a memorable thing. 

— H. Caldwell

source_en:
I have a strange paralysis. Like I don’t know where to start. 
It tingles really as it takes control. The red veins outlining the pace of my heart, the quickening of my pulse. 
My master calls to me.
From the other side. 
Where he awaits a door.
The door is ours door to build. The door is my task.
Under the guidance of Lord Felwyl we shall build
a door of many hands, intertwined, all outstretched together in welcoming. 
Hands of the working folk. Hands of the non-believers. Hands of the unwilling.
One taste of the bloom and they move together, molding and forming into one, bodies becoming a single, purified organism, and their hands reach, reaching, stretching and ripping and breaking together in unison, to welcome your second coming, my Lord. 
Together as one.
They reach from the red bloom.
Yes. That’s it. 
I know exactly where to start. 
Thank you master. 
You shall have your door soon.

Ornate gauntlets once belonging to a knight in service to House Haedrik from the western lands of Armaea.

The Haedriks fled the Armaen political theatre in pursuit of new beginnings and economic supremacy. source_en:
Once more, I am roused from my sleep by gut-wrenching nightmares. The frequency is now unbearable, and I can no longer sustain my life this way.

Again I find myself in the graveyard behind St. Uriel’s chapel, under that same accursed crimson moonlight basking the yard in an ethereal haze.

There, cloaked men gathered around that rotten, gnarled tree, whispering profane and terrible things before a woman chained to its trunk. Suddenly, I am taken behind her eyes, and I witness the men brandish a knife.

I am spared witness to the bloodshed, but I cannot help but feel it's true.

Why am I seeing this?

source_en:
Welcome to the Crimson Moon's Summer Build!

This demo reflects the current state of team's development towards our First Playable milestone later this year. In this play session you will be slaying monsters, scavenging for gear, leveling your Nephilim, and more while exploring the first of the two areas we are building as part of this gate.

Thank you for taking the time to play our game and share your feedback with us! We look forward to sharing our progress in the coming months.

- Team Metal
